newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand faces new polls as parliament dissolved.
newsitem.headline: Thailand faces new polls as parliament dissolved.

text.p: Thailand's King Bhumibol Adulyadej issued a royal proclamation on Friday dissolving parliament and setting November 17 as the date for fresh elections, state-owned Radio Thailand said.
The proclamation was made more than an hour after a deputy premier and close ally of the outgoing Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa told reporters a dissolution was to be announced.
Banharn went on television soon after the royal proclamation to explain the reasons for his surprise decision to dissolve parliament and call a snap election.
He had been widely expected to quit after promising to resign under pressure from key allies in his six-party coalition government.
The allies had sought his resignation in return for their support for him at a parliamentary no-confidence vote which Banharn later won. But he effectively lost his job.
Leaders of Banharn's 14-month-old, six-party coalition had been huddling in deep discussion since last Saturday trying to find a replacement for Banharn.
But Banharn avoided their meetings, keeping his cards close to his chest.

"The process of selecting my successor could not take place smoothly. And it is generally believed that a multi-party coalition government could lead to conflicts and political problems...," Banharn said.
"I therefore see it appropriate to dissolve the house so as to return the important mandate of political determination to the people at this turning point," he added.
He promised to be an honest caretaker prime minister and said he would supervise a new election fairly.
Many politicians and analysts were surprised by Banharn's move because they had expected Defence Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh to succeed him.
But Banharn's supporters in the main Chart Thai party refused to support Chavalit who they saw as as the man who engineered the premier's downfall.
